intro: Anesthesiologist assistants monitor patients closely and act fast during procedures, skills shared by imaging and surgical technology careers. The closest of the 25 careers below are cardiovascular technology and surgical assisting, both at a 75% skill match, and every option needs no more education than you already have.
why_it_works: Each case means preparing equipment, watching vital signs minute by minute and reacting quickly when a patient's condition changes. O*NET rates judgment at 3.62 out of 5 for this job and operations monitoring at 3.5. Imaging, nuclear medicine and surgical roles use the same vigilance. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470 and are a 69% match, the best-paid option here.
Nuclear Medicine Technologists earn $101,370 and use your monitoring and safety skills.
Teaching in health programs is a 63% match with a median of $107,310.

faq.q: What jobs can former anesthesiologist assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are cardiovascular technologists and technicians (75%), Surgical Assistants (75%) and radiologic technologists (72%), based on O*NET 31.0. Nuclear Medicine Technologists are also 72% matched and earn $101,370, according to BLS May 2025 data, and use the same careful patient monitoring.

faq.q: Which jobs for anesthesiologist assistants pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Medical Dosimetrists at $147,470, postsecondary health specialties teachers at $107,310 and medical scientists at $103,410, according to BLS May 2025 data. BLS reports anesthesiologist assistants within a broader group, so compare with your own pay.

faq.q: Do anesthesiologist assistants need more education to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than anesthesiologist assistants already have, including all of the top 10. An associate degree is common in the closest match, held by 63% of workers, though imaging jobs need their own certification.

faq.q: What skills should anesthesiologist assistants learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are repairing, equipment maintenance, managing materials and persuasion. Complex problem solving already rates 3.38 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so equipment and technical knowledge is the main step toward imaging and device roles.
